title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC vs Pighius — hereditary vice proximate death-cause
pass_a_gloss: That is Pighius, Catharinus, and Salmeron's view, rightly damned by our Churches. If you grant infants an inherent original vice that is truly sin, enough to damn the race and make womb-hidden infants guilty of eternal death, why does 'hereditarily inherent vice is their death-cause' not answer why they die? That names the proximate cause; Adam's fall is the remote.
pass_b_english: Which was the opinion of Pighius and Catharinus and Salmeron, rightly condemned by our Churches: for if you believe there is in infants an original inherent vice which is truly sin, which suffices for damning the human race, which makes infants hiding in the maternal womb guilty of eternal death before God—why, when you ask why infants die, does it not satisfy the one who answers that in them the cause of death is the vice or sin hereditarily inherent? For this is to give the proximate cause of infants' death, whose remote cause is Adam's fall.
source_text: Quae Pighii & Catharini, & Salmeronis fuit sententia ab Ecclesiis nostris iure damnata: nam si credis in infantibus vitium esse originale inhaerens, quod vere peccatum sit, quod generi humano damnando sufficiat, quod infantes in utero materno delitescentes aeternae mortis reos coram Deo peragat, cur tibi quaerenti, cur infantes moriantur, non satisfacit qui respondet, in illis causam esse mortis vitium seu peccatum hereditario inhaerens? Hoc enim est mortis infantium proximam causam afferre, cuius remota est lapsus Adami.

choices.choice: Pighius line condemned; hereditary vice proximate infant-death cause
